messages.author: cb02869ed20f9a2b
messages.subject: PCA from trajectory.analysis
parts:
Dear all,
I have a doubt regarding the plot of the PCA resulting from the "trajectory.analysis". We are using the "trajectory.analysis" function to compare the sexual dimorphism among five different species. If I have understood properly when we perform the analysis we obtain the plot of the between-group PCA, in which the trajectories of the five species are shown (see attached figure). These trajectories are the vectors between the means of females and males (white and black dots respectively) . However, these means do not match with the means of PC1 and PC2 of the between-group PCA (we have specifically calculated these means). My question is to which means correspond the white and black dots? We know that the trajectory analysis is not only performed with PC1 and PC2, but with all geometric information, is this the cause for the lack of correspondence between black and white dots and the means of the between-group PCA?
Thanks in advance for your help.
Best regards,
Francesc

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] PCA from trajectory.analysis
parts:
Francesc,

You did not include information about how you set up your trajectory analysis or how you performed your between-group PCA; therefore it is not possible to reconcile how results might be different.  There are various possible reasons for analytical differences, including:

- covariates in the trajectory analysis
- different scaling of eigenvectors
- arbitrary flipping of eigenvectors
- weighting of covariance matrix
- different methods of calculating (or miscalculating) means

Note that if you used something like the groupPCA function in Morpho, the default uses weighting of a group covariance matrix for predefined groups.  morphol.disparity obtains least-squares means from a factorial model (possibly with covariates), if specified that way, but does not have any input for weighting.  If one wanted to perform a weighted between-group PCA, they could use the $means output from trajectory.analysis and follow the format for eigen-analysis used in groupPCA, using that script.

For trajectory.analysis, we perform the between-group PCA, simply as,

pca.means <- prcomp(means)
pc.means <- pca.means$x
pc.data <- center(Y)%*%pca.means$rotation,

which can be found by looking at the code.  You can see there is no strange manipulation, but “means” can be least-squares means if there were covariates in the trajectory.analysis, which will be different than calculating means by group (as groupPCA does).

Hope that helps.
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] PCA from trajectory.analysis
parts:
Ian,

That is an internal function but could be called with

geomorph:::center()

Alternatively, and under most circumstances, you can use the scale function, with the argument scale = FALSE. They both do the same thing but scale has error traps and other bells and whistles That makes for a slow function when thousands of permutations are used.  Our center function is a faster function with a simple single purpose that enhances coding efficiency and other functions.  But it neither has a help page nor is intended for general use.

I was revealing our code more so than suggesting what to do by hand. 

Hope that is helpful. 
Mike

Sent from my iPhone
